newsitem.title: UKRAINE: AGROKHLEB - Ukraine 97 grain output up, quality down.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB - Ukraine 97 grain output up, quality down.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union, in association with Ukragroconsult, a private Ukrainian agricultural consultancy based in Kiev.
UKRAINE: GRAIN OUTPUT SEEN UP IN 1997, QUALITY DOWN
KIEV, Aug 4 - The area sown to grain and pulses increased 22 percent in 1997 from 1996, with the most significant growth in corn, millet and winter barley plantings.
Sunseed plantings rose only 2.0 percent, while sugarbeet shrank almost 10 percent.
Harvesting progressed slowly in July, and by the end of the month, the harvested area was only half 1996 levels.

About 90 percent of the harvested area to date is located in the south of Ukraine so far. Harvesting has not yet started in Forest-Steppe and Polesye regions, accounting for over 50 percent of total acreage to be harvested.

Grain quality has suffered due to heavy rains, with protein and starch content seriously reduced. The bulk of the harvested wheat is rated fifth grade, which requires blending with high quality wheat.
The initial forecast of milling wheat production of 7.0-8.0 million tonnes has been revised downwards by 0.8-1.0 million tonnes.
